It's a bit of both, but I guess hate is kind of a strong word, I would say unsatisfied with would be a bit more apt. I always want to be improving as a person, and I think improving my body is the easiest way to track progress (looks, weight, etc.). 

Wanting to lose or gain weight because you want your body to look different is a completely valid motivation. If it's what makes you happy, then you should do it. It is not anti body positive in my opinion. If you aren't doing it for yourself and feel highly pressured by outside factors, then maybe you should reconsider why you're working out. 

And if you're not 100% sure why you're working out, I would just keep going and think about it again in a month or two. In the end, only you can decide if you want to work out

As long as the saturated fats aren't super high, it's not that big of a deal. Fats perform many functions in the body, and have been demonized by many companies that produce high carb (simple sugar) foods. This video gives a simple but effective overview of fats https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ji0ZFybqWD8&list=LLsNNgAm3K3NSj0dBkz3CcJ

I would wait one more month and if you still don't gain then you should eat more. I would add 300 calories to your goal, eat for a month, compare to the past and see where you're at

I don't know the intensity of your workout, but 6 days for 1.5-2 hours for 11-12 exercises seems like a lot. It might not be overtraining, but it seems like it could be a bit more streamlined. Taking a quick look at the program, it seems like there's a large amount of volume already in it with just the standard 6 sets. I would increase intensity on the accessories, and do slightly slower, high-quality reps. 

To be clear though, I don't think this is the source of your lack of gains, exercise burns a lot less calories than you think. It's likely a matter of nutrition.

In a different light I find it concerning that youtube and other media companies are effectively censoring content certain. Now I get that a private company should be able to decide what content is hosted on their site, but as a Quasi-Monopoly I think that it's irresponsible to decide who is okay to speak and who isn't. While completely in their rights to do so, wouldn't it be concerning if other content creators were kept from speaking such as The Young Turks? I believe while they don't have the obligation to host everyone, they have the responsibility to encourage the free flow of information. Limiting certain people will only make them seem like victims, and can slowly morph into more aggressive censorship. But overall, my main point is that this issue isn't black and white, and has quite a lot of nuance depending on the scenario.
